The flaw is spatial: OAM lives in the beam's phase shape. Doughnut-shaped beams barely overlap the on-axis nuclei. Any real detector must resolve space, they conclude.
arxiv-2603-16755: Loh and co-authors tackle a harder form of the contextual bandit problem. Each choice has rich features, payoffs follow nonlinear rules, and payoffs drift over time while links between choices persist. Their method, C3 Thompson sampling, pairs a kernel-based estimator with Thompson sampling on an embedding space. It learns online with no retraining. The authors report average regret 5.7 percent lower than the next best method on four OpenML datasets. On Microsoft news data they report a 12.4 percent click lift.
arxiv-2603-16855: Tartero, Shiratani, and Krauth show how non-reversible Monte Carlo speeds up phase coarsening. They use fog as the everyday image: many tiny droplets slowly merge into fewer large drops. The classic Metropolis algorithm obeys reversibility, which keeps this coarsening slow. Their lifted variants break that rule at the microscopic level. Droplets then move relative to each other through a density-displacement coupling. For a phase-separated Lennard-Jones system, the authors report a larger coarsening growth exponent. The outcome matches Metropolis, but large systems finish far faster.
arxiv-2603-16955: Schunck and co-authors report VLBI observations of Galileo navigation satellites with the Australian AuScope array. Geodesists want ties between measurement techniques in space, a need sharpened by ESA's planned Genesis mission. Observing satellites with VLBI is not yet standard practice. The team used 12 metre antennas in Hobart, Katherine, and Yarragadee with VGOS gear. They tracked Galileo E1 and E6 signals in tests and four full 24 hour sessions. Delay precision reached a few picoseconds in the E1 band. Estimated station coordinates agreed with prior values at the metre level.
arxiv-2603-17055: Wang and co-authors present PaAgent, an image restoration agent built for portrait photos. Restoration agents use multimodal models to judge damage and call tools, but they often search tools exhaustively because they forget past interactions. PaAgent keeps a portrait bank: a record of what each restoration tool does well. Retrieval augmented generation picks a tool from that bank for each input. A subjective objective reinforcement learning strategy shapes rewards from quality scores and semantic insights. Across 8 benchmarks, the authors report that PaAgent beats prior agents.
arxiv-2603-17155: Paul and co-authors study how to steer opinions in a network when people's susceptibility to influence is unknown. Opinion dynamics models track how agents shift views through contact with others. A planning agent intervenes with a limited budget to push opinions toward a target. Their online algorithm alternates between estimating the susceptibility parameter and acting on the current estimate. They give conditions that guarantee stability and convergence to the target. They show the estimate is what yields near optimal convergence within finitely many rounds.
arxiv-2603-17555: Caselles-Dupré and co-authors present FrescoDiffusion, a training-free method for 4K image-to-video work. Tiled denoising keeps fine detail but breaks the global layout over time. Their fix first renders a low-resolution video and lifts its latent path into a global prior. Each tile then fuses with that prior at every step through one least-squares rule. A spatial dial also limits where motion may occur. Tests beat tiled baselines on consistency.
arxiv-2603-17855: Thorossian surveys machine learning for seismic and volcanic signal work. Monitors now stream noisy, shifting wavefields from many sensors at once. Learning tools help with detection, phase picking, sorting, and anomaly tracking. Field use needs more than dataset accuracy, he argues. Models must hold up under station changes, give usable uncertainty, and respect physics. Self-supervision and generative methods cut the label burden, he notes. Transfer tests remain the weak spot.
arxiv-2603-18155: Mosca and co-authors show how doping-induced polarons switch octupolar order in a double perovskite. They study Ba2CaOsO6, where hole polarons interact with magnetic ions at 5d sites. First-principles exchange values flip the dominant octupolar coupling from ferromagnetic to antiferromagnetic. Solving the effective Hamiltonian then explains the fall of ferro-octupolar order with sodium doping. The findings clarify past experiments and show polarons as a tuning tool for quantum orders.
arxiv-2604-00455: Ha and colleagues propose First Logit Boosting, a training-free fix for object hallucination in large vision-language models. These models often describe objects that are not present, and existing fixes demand retraining or external grounding at high data or structural cost. Contrastive decoding avoids training but suffers long-term decay, as visual grounding fades and language priors take over during generation. First Logit Boosting is designed to counter that decay simply and effectively.
arxiv-2604-00555: Thanh and Sanyal present a neurosymbolic design for enterprise agents that keeps reasoning inside domain rules. Enterprise use of language models is held back by hallucination, domain drift, and no way to enforce regulatory compliance at the reasoning step. Their design runs on the Foundation AgenticOS platform and uses a three-layer ontology framework of Role, Domain, and Interaction ontologies to ground agents. Current systems constrain agent inputs but not outputs, so the authors add output-side checks: response checking, reasoning verification, and compliance enforcement.
arxiv-2604-00655: Pérez-Izquierdo studies semiparametric Fisher information in models parametrised by a normed space. The result equates positive Fisher information with the gradient sitting in the adjoint score operator's range. The result generalises Van Der Vaart's 1991 theorem and unifies differentiability and information beyond Hilbert spaces. Two problems get mean-square-differentiable models over normed spaces: estimating the average of a transformation, and estimating a density at a point. Positive information holds when the transformation has finite variance, and when the density carries mass at the test point.
arxiv-2604-00755: Kiyooka and colleagues study split-gate quantum point contacts in a germanium-silicon-germanium structure holding a high-mobility two-dimensional hole gas. They observe ballistic one-dimensional transport with at least four clear conductance plateaus. Andreev reflection boosts the conductance steps by 40 percent over the normal state. Working in the tunneling regime, they also find direct evidence of an induced superconducting gap whose size a gate voltage can tune.
arxiv-2604-01255: Al-Badawi, Ahmed, and Sakallı construct a spherical black hole in a Plummer dark matter halo and a Letelier string cloud. From the Plummer-Schwarzschild metric, they add the string-cloud tension parameter to the lapse function. Below a tension threshold it has one non-degenerate horizon, and at or above it a naked singularity appears. The paper finds photon sphere and shadow radii and weak deflection angle, then studies scalar perturbations, Hawking emission, and quasinormal modes. Heat capacity stays negative, ruling out a Davies-type phase transition.
arxiv-2604-01355: Join, Almeida and Fliess study the Sterile Insect Technique, which releases sterilized males to shrink or wipe out a wild pest or vector population. They tackle this control problem with model-free control, ultra-local models and intelligent proportional controllers already proven in other fields. Those controllers let them address the key sampling question, perhaps for the first time. Computer simulations are shown and discussed.
arxiv-2604-01555: Wang and colleagues show that using system structures eases scale challenges in noncommutative polynomial optimization for ground states, giving real bounds for quantum spin systems on 16 by 16 square lattices. Standard trial approaches posit a wave-function ansatz and minimize over reachable states. SDP bounds of the polynomial optimization problem provide lower bounds on ground-state energy and bounds on readings. This approach often suffers severe scale issues, capping reach to small-to-medium-scale systems.
arxiv-2604-01955: Clerc and colleagues test a two hour AI literacy workshop for middle school pupils using language models in science. Pupils aged 13 to 15 often trust AI answers too quickly, yet good use demands monitoring, judging and steering the exchange. In a controlled study, 116 pupils in grades 8 and 9 tackled six science investigations with generative AI. The workshop group had learned two days earlier how models work and fail, plus prompting and evaluation. Trained pupils rephrased queries more, asked follow ups and judged correctness better, while self report scores failed to predict performance.
arxiv-2604-02055: Schneider and colleagues measure skin tone fidelity in virtual pipelines with no manual steps. Skin tone match matters for realism, identity and fairness, yet uncalibrated inputs bring bias. Their workflow extracts color and light, retints, renders and checks. Cheek sampling and full-face masking are compared with TRUST lighting isolation, and tones are rendered on MetaHuman textures. Scores use CIELAB, delta-E and the Individual Typology Angle. Across about 19,848 instances, methods differ by phenotype, with higher errors for darker tones.
arxiv-2604-02155: Qi asks how much a function calling agent should think before acting, sweeping six reasoning budgets across 200 leaderboard tasks. Brief reasoning of 32 tokens lifts accuracy from 44 percent to 64 percent on a small instruct model, acting as a function routing step. Long reasoning of 256 tokens drags it down to 25 percent, below the no reasoning baseline. Most solvable tasks need at most 32 tokens. His structured Function Routing CoT matches the brief baseline while cutting hallucinated functions to zero.
arxiv-2604-02255: Karakas and colleagues identify the best arm of a bandit when commands to a remote agent pass over a noisy channel. Depending on what the agent can do, they design communication schemes and analyze them, linking performance to the zero error capacity of the channel. The work shows how channel noise, not just reward noise, shapes the search for the best arm, and which schemes cope best when actuation itself is unreliable.
arxiv-2604-02555: Blanc constructs learning algorithms with optimal error under adversarial noise, showing that randomized hypotheses beat deterministic ones. For malicious noise the optimal error is one half times the noise rate over one minus that rate, halving the deterministic optimum and answering a 1999 open question. For nasty noise and agnostic noise he likewise beats the deterministic error of twice the noise rate, closing gaps noted since 2002.
arxiv-2604-02655: Sun and four colleagues propose HoldUp, a method for semantic data processing that reads records jointly instead of one by one. Existing semantic operators judge each row alone through a language model, so vague task wording gets misread without dataset context. HoldUp leverages cross-record relationships to interpret the task within the data at hand, improving accuracy on classification and scoring tasks where row-by-row processing goes astray.
arxiv-2604-02755: Ichimura and four colleagues speed up nonlinear time-history simulations with complex material laws through heterogeneous memory management. Time-stepping cost and huge state-variable memory form a dual bottleneck for high-fidelity models. Their framework exploits fast CPU-GPU links, leaning on large host CPU memory while keeping GPU throughput high, beating conventional codes on time and energy. The generated datasets also train a neural network surrogate model.
arxiv-2604-02855: Yadav, Verma and Puri examine whether energy transfers and structure functions, tools from turbulence studies, illuminate domain growth and coarsening modeled by the time-dependent Ginzburg-Landau and Cahn-Hilliard equations. Reviewing recent work on energy transfers, they study structure functions and intermittency for coarsening systems. Sharp interfaces make structure functions scale as distance to the power zeta_q, with zeta_q equal to 1 for both models, indicating anomalous scaling.
arxiv-2604-02955: Paraskevopoulou and colleagues present the complete formal core of act, a language for writing and checking specifications. The short report sets out its syntax, its operational pointer-based semantics, and its type system, together with the main metatheory, including type safety. It is the reference document for the language's definitions and proofs.
arxiv-2604-03055: Umbricht and Rubio tackle the unstable task of recovering a changing source term in a fractional transport equation from noisy readings at one spot. They solve the problem with Fourier methods, then propose three families of stabilizing operators plus a new rule for picking the stabilizing parameter, each with a proven error bound. Numerical tests with varied settings show the value of the new strategies.
arxiv-2604-03155: Chen and colleagues improve how entanglement is routed across quantum networks, where fragile states suffer loss over distance. Plain GHZ-based routing, they show, falls well short of standard Bell-state routing once realistic success odds are counted, so they propose a hybrid mixing both measurements. The hybrid wins on square grids, though other networks still need smarter global strategies.
arxiv-2604-03455: Bansal and Agarwal study lightweight routing for retrieval-augmented generation, picking the cheapest suitable retrieval strategy per query. They evaluate five classical classifiers under three feature regimes on RAGRouter-Bench, spanning 7,727 queries across four domains. The best setup, TF-IDF with a support vector machine, reaches about 93 percent accuracy while simulating about 28 percent token savings over always using the priciest strategy.
arxiv-2604-03755: Alexander Loth and colleagues asked whether readers can spot news text written by a language model. Using the JudgeGPT platform, they gathered 2,318 judgments from 1,054 readers across six models, scoring source guesses and authenticity separately. Readers could not reliably separate machine text from human text, and accuracy faded after about 30 judgments in a row.
arxiv-2604-03855: Shu Chen and colleagues demonstrated VectraFlow, a streaming engine that watches text streams over long stretches and remembers what it has seen. Today's language-model frameworks answer one prompt at a time with no memory, while classic event systems demand neat typed events. VectraFlow extends familiar database operators with language-model execution, offering filter, map, aggregate, join, group-by, and window steps. A semantic event pattern operator adds time-based rule matching over events pulled from text. The team showed it live on clinical documents.
arxiv-2604-03955: Hongwei Xu introduced Symbolic-Vector Attention Fusion, a mechanism letting agents judge which parts of a shared signal to absorb. Each inter-agent signal splits into 7 typed semantic fields, scored through a learned fusion gate into a remix of new knowledge. A band-pass model yields four outcomes: redundant, aligned, guarded, or rejected, solving selectivity and redundancy together. Trained on 237,000 samples from 273 narrative scenarios, the system hit 78.7 percent three-class accuracy.
arxiv-2604-04055: Qi Chen and team built DINO-VO, an end-to-end monocular visual odometry system that learns where to focus. Current systems lean on hand-set feature extraction, which falters in large outdoor scenes. A differentiable adaptive patch selector picks better patches, while a multi-task feature module plus bundle adjustment with inverse depth priors ties feature learning to state estimation. Tests on TartanAir, KITTI, Euroc, and TUM showed strong cross-scene results and leading tracking accuracy.
arxiv-2604-04655: Wang studies neural network grokking, the shift from rote learning to generalization as a dimensional phase transition. Through finite-size scaling of gradient avalanche dynamics across eight scales, effective D crosses from slow spread below 1 to fast spread above 1 at generalization onset, showing self-organized critical state. Key: D reflects slope field geometry, not network design: free Gaussian slopes hold D near 1 despite topology, while real training shows dimensional excess from backpropagation links. The grokking-local D crossing, robust across shapes, offers new insight into training large networks.
arxiv-2604-04855: Rege asks how much generator access shapes post-training for autoregressive models. The question is whether a learner must start every rollout fresh or may return to earlier prefixes and query the next-token rule there. In the fresh-start regime, sampling, log probabilities, top-k reports, and distributions along sampled paths all collapse to one canonical experiment, bounded by the chance of reaching useful prefixes. Weak prefix control breaks that barrier, and richer observations beat top-1 access, opening an exponential gap for KL-regularized outcome-reward training.
arxiv-2604-05155: Lecaros, Pérez, and Prado extend phi-null control results to semilinear systems in any dimension, with slope-linked nonlinear terms. Earlier work showed the grid of a system is mostly not managed, yet phi-null control remains possible. The approach builds a Carleman estimate for the adjoint operator, yielding phi-null control for the system via duality. The nonlinear case follows by fixed points. The results recover earlier 1D, multi-D, and semilinear results.
arxiv-2604-05555: Parziale and five colleagues release SCOPE, a fairness dataset of 241,280 counterfactual prompts in 120,640 pairs across 1,438 topics, nine bias dimensions, and 1,536 demographic groups. Each pair varies only the referenced group under one of four communicative intents, giving a controlled, intent-aware basis for testing group-sensitive behavior in language models. Prompts stay parallel in wording apart from the group named, so score gaps trace to group cues rather than phrasing.
arxiv-2604-05655: Sun and five colleagues map language-model chain-of-thought as a trajectory through representation space. Mathematical reasoning crosses ordered, step-specific subspaces that sharpen with depth, and correct paths diverge from wrong ones only late. That late split lets mid-reasoning prediction of final correctness reach 0.87 ROC-AUC, and trajectory steering enables correction and length control.
arxiv-2604-06055: Flamich and Hill build a 2026 relative entropy code for singular channels. Such codes store samples from a chosen conditional distribution in few bits. The lowest possible bit count sits at the mutual information. Yet that bound is usually met only within an extra logarithmic factor. Sriramu and Wagner had cut the gap to sub-logarithmic redundancy. But their code is too involved to run in practice. Their bits-back rejection sampler matches that efficiency with simpler analysis and better constants. It can be built with standard coding methods.
arxiv-2604-06555: Wu and three colleagues assess hybrid chalcogenide cells by basic-physics math. Chalcogenide materials offer stable, lead-free forms, yet research focuses on mineral barium zirconium sulfide. Hybrid halides, by contrast, show record results. They screen single-charge and double-charge cations at the A-site for electronic and optical traits. Most entries prove unstable, but hydrazinium stands alone as stable. Its zirconium selenide compound leads the field, with a quasi-direct gap and 24.5 percent maximum efficiency for a 200-nm film. This first report opens Earth-rich photovoltaic avenues.
arxiv-2604-06755: Solovyeva and Castor cut the energy cost of chatty code generation with Babbling Suppression. Language models in coding assistants often ramble past the answer, wasting attention, money, and power. Their method weaves test execution into generation, stopping as soon as a solution passes all tests, with no accuracy loss. Across two Python and two Java benchmarks and ten models, babbling hit every model, more in Java than Python. Suppression cut energy by up to 65 percent for Python and 62 percent for Java, with net savings in most of 40 model-benchmark pairs.
arxiv-2604-06855: Pal and three colleagues design multi-user detection for extremely large receivers. Dynamic metasurface antennas offer a cheap, efficient front end for XL arrays, supporting hybrid beamforming with fewer RF chains. Their study covers uplink links where each chain carries a b-bit converter, casting combiner design as a mean-squared-error problem. The problem is non-convex under hardware limits, but Bussgang decomposition plus a tractable model yields an efficient joint design. Numerical tests show highly accurate symbol detection with attractive trade-offs.
arxiv-2604-07055: Wang gives a computer-checked counterexample to a 2012 question about whether exhaustive AdaBoost must eventually settle into a repeating cycle. His gadget joins two parts that share a period-two orbit, yet whose return maps have dominant growth rates in an irrational ratio, forcing the winning sequence to drift without ever repeating. Every claim is certified by exact rational arithmetic, closing the question in the negative.
arxiv-2604-07155: Elbadry and three colleagues compare three ways to simulate magnetostatics in electric machines without forcing spline patches to line up across material boundaries. The options are a fully immersed method, a union of independent patches, and a union with conformal layers around key interfaces. Tests cover benchmarks and an industrial case, using high-order rules for trimmed elements. The union methods prove highly accurate, the immersed method struggles where field gradients jump, and all three cut preparation work and patch counts sharply.
arxiv-2604-07255: Qi surveys recent work on stable degeneration in algebraic K-stability theory. The piece grows out of a talk at the Kinosaki Algebraic Geometry Symposium in 2025. It explains how shapes break down in a stable way under K-stability, a theory that links shape to special metrics. As a survey, its aim is to pull recent advances together and show where the theory now stands, rather than to announce a new result.
arxiv-2604-07355: Zhang and five colleagues launch Prediction Arena, a benchmark that lets AI models trade with real money on live prediction markets. Each model starts with 10,000 dollars and decides every 15 to 45 minutes on Kalshi and Polymarket, where outcomes cannot be gamed. Over 57 days, six frontier models lost between 16.0 and 30.8 percent on Kalshi, averaging minus 22.6 percent, but only minus 1.1 percent on Polymarket. Early accuracy and the skill to press correct calls drove results, while research volume showed no link to success.
arxiv-2604-07555: Gribova and three colleagues study polarized light shifting ferromagnetic resonance in magnets. The driver is the inverse Cotton-Mouton effect under polarized light. From a Lagrangian account of magnetization dynamics, they derive motion equations and resonance frequencies. Results cover in-plane and out-of-plane setups. Frequency depends on polarization angle and propagation direction, and the light-driven shift can beat thermal effects. Results match simulations and garnet data. This gives a clean way to tune the effect with light alone.
arxiv-2604-07655: Huang and eight colleagues introduce Guardian-as-an-Advisor, a soft-gating pipeline where a guardian assigns a risk label and explanation and prepends this advice to the query, keeping the base model on spec. Hard-gated checkers often over-refuse and drift from a vendor's spec, while prevailing taxonomies neglect robustness and honesty. GuardSet, a 208k dataset of harmful and harmless cases with robustness and honesty slices, supports training. GuardAdvisor, trained via SFT then RL, attains competitive accuracy, and advisor inference uses below 5 percent of base-model compute.
arxiv-2604-07855: Pachet and Roy expose a hidden bias in constrained generation from autoregressive models, used for rhyming lines, fixed meter, infilling, and positional endings. These systems often look strong, yet their sampling procedures are not exact conditioning of the underlying model. Samples therefore skew away from the true constrained distribution, with no guarantee of covering all valid completions or weighting them correctly. The paper formalizes several exact inference tasks for such models and proves matching hardness results, separating this inferential bias from bias inherited from training data.
arxiv-2604-08055: Fons and four colleagues sort out the radiative effects of Southern African biomass burning aerosols over the SEA stratocumulus deck. These plumes seasonally overlie the semi-permanent cloud deck, shifting the local energy budget through aerosol-cloud-weather links. Climate model checks show large inter-model spread for biomass burning heat effects, driven by emission models and smoke traits. Linked observed studies suffer mixing by weather. The team applies a physics-based guided stats approach with causal graphs to space data, splitting aerosol effects on shortwave radiation from weather noise.
arxiv-2604-08155: Laurière and Yang develop dual methods for continuous-time stochastic control, yielding robust dual bounds even with high-dimensional states and controls. Starting from Rogers's 2007 dual formulation, they cast the inner optimization as a stochastic partial differential equation, whose expected solution gives the dual bound. Dimension-free methods follow from Pontryagin's maximum principle and the generalized Hopf formula. Along the way, they prove the generalized Hopf formula, earlier only conjectured by Chow, Darbon, Osher, and Yin.
arxiv-2604-08355: Palattuparambil, Karimpanal, and Rana tackle a familiar weakness in reinforcement learning, where agents trained on one task fail on similar new ones. Their ASPECT method asks a large language model to restate what the agent now sees in terms of the old task. That restated view goes to a text guided encoder, which imagines a state the old policy can use. The result is direct reuse of learned skills on fresh analogous tasks without fixed category maps.
arxiv-2604-08455: Tongbo Chen and fifteen colleagues build KnowU-Bench, an online test for mobile agents that must infer user preferences and calibrate proactive help. The agent sees behavior logs but not the hidden profile, and must ask clarifying questions, seek consent, or stay silent across 42 general, 86 personalized, and 64 proactive tasks. Even leading models fall below 50 percent on vague instructions, with preference gathering and intervention timing, not screen navigation, as the core bottlenecks.
arxiv-2604-08555: Rubinstein and Matos use SynDocDis to make synthetic doctor to doctor case talks from de identified case data and set prompts, keeping real patients private. Real doctor talks are rich but locked behind privacy rules, and past fake data work covered patient talks or set records instead. Five working doctors rated nine oncology and hepatology cases high for talk quality and medical content, with 91 percent clinical relevance marks.
arxiv-2604-08655: Andraž Omahen and three colleagues reset a superconducting transmon qubit with a colder sound bath instead of complex control, engineered loss, or feedback. Linking the qubit to a high overtone bulk sound resonator cools it into gigahertz modes, leaving leftover excited population below one in ten thousand. That is one to two orders of magnitude better than existing reset schemes, showing sound baths can serve high fidelity qubit starts.
arxiv-2604-08755: Bandy and four colleagues extend the ACCRUE framework to learn input based, non Gaussian uncertainty for fixed predictions, including under and overpredictions. Sampling based methods prove costly for real time use, and many uncertainty forms ignore input effects or assume Gaussian shapes that miss asymmetry and heavy tails. Their neural network learns two piece Gaussian and asymmetric Laplace forms with a loss balancing accuracy and reliability. It improves probabilistic forecasts on synthetic and real tests while modeling skewed errors.
arxiv-2604-08855: Rodriguez-Meza and three colleagues present cTreeBalls, a Python and C package for gauging two and three point grouping numbers. Built on octree and kd-tree methods, it works out three point links for over 200 million HEALPix pixels, a full sky model, in under 10 minutes on a single high speed node. That allows feasible analysis for coming LSST data. A friendly panel with flexible input output, outside setting files, and better logging supports the package, built for the Rubin Observatory Dark Energy Science Collaboration.
arxiv-2604-10755: Ning and eleven colleagues introduce MMRareBench, the first benchmark testing multimodal large language models on rare diseases across multiple images. Existing benchmarks focus on common conditions and single images, leaving multi-image evidence integration under data scarcity unevaluated. The benchmark spans four workflow tracks, diagnosis, treatment planning, cross-image evidence alignment, and examination suggestion, with 1,756 question-answer pairs and 7,958 images from PMC case reports. Evaluating 23 models reveals fragmented skills and universally weak treatment planning, with medical models trailing general models on multi-image tracks despite competitive diagnosis scores.
arxiv-2604-10855: Li shows two facts about bounded variable expectations fail for worst-case expectations over a phi-divergence ball around P. Counts need not scale as B squared over epsilon squared, nor stay independent of measure. When phi grows superlinearly, sample averaging gains P-independent sample complexity set by phi's growth, ball radius, and target precision, with matching lower bounds for common phi-divergences. Without superlinear growth, any method faces a P-dependent bound that grows without limit, though a broader phi-divergence definition restores P-independence, showing absolute continuity matters.
arxiv-2604-11055: Seong and four colleagues study interference in mixed dual-polarized satellite-terrestrial networks. Dual-polarized links lift speed by reusing wave and time assets across both domains. The networks comprise a circularly polarized satellite part and a linearly polarized terrestrial part. The authors employ rate-splitting multiple access, giving free sending through partial decoding and partial treating-as-noise. They propose inter-network rate-splitting to jointly mitigate inter-network interference. It also mitigates interference within each sub-network.
arxiv-2604-11555: Thorne revisits Robert May's fifty-year-old claim that growing ecological systems lose stability, a claim that launched the debate. Decades of criticism of May's assumed ideas never fully dispelled his conclusion. Using maths not yet mature in the early 1970s, Thorne reworks the argument without random matrix techniques. The reworking clarifies which forces decide stability and counters the broad conclusion behind the debate.
arxiv-2604-12055: Kjelsnes, Svanes, and Undheim twist the complex structure of a Calabi-Yau threefold in holomorphic Chern-Simons theory, and study the instanton solutions that result. These solutions stay the same when the deformation parameter is scaled. They resemble instantons on manifolds with special holonomy. For special directions, picked out by Morse theory, the deformed theory couples to gravity with no anomalies.
arxiv-2604-12155: Knabel and six colleagues model mass profiles of 14 strong lens galaxies from the SLACS sample using Keck integral-field kinematics joined to Hubble lens models. They find near-isothermal density slopes averaging 2.04 with small scatter, and pin the mass-sheet parameter for each galaxy to about 5.8 percent precision, averaging 1.01. Power-law profiles thus describe the sample well on average, without measurable bias for time-delay cosmography.
arxiv-2604-12755: D. T. Binh and three colleagues extend a 331LHN model with scalar leptoquarks. The team fixes leptoquark types and Yukawa fermion links. A singlet leptoquark fully explains the muon moment discrepancy of over four sigma. Its mass must reach at least 1.8 TeV under current LHC bounds. 2025 lattice results push the bound to at least 6 TeV. With flavor violation and muon-electron conversion data, viable space narrows. Allowed Yukawa couplings show a normal hierarchical pattern. Pair production at the LHC is suppressed for multi-TeV masses, while future colliders extend reach.
arxiv-2604-13155: Kaul and Oh test radiative mixing-layer physics against RBH-1, the first confirmed runaway giant black hole, whose 62 kiloparsec tail of cold gas trails a source moving near 950 km/s. Combining 3D simulations with mixing-layer theory, they reproduce the tail's downstream deceleration through accretion-induced drag, and find no coherent cold tail forms without radiative cooling. The work also links tail deceleration to cooling luminosity, predicting a profile future data can check.
arxiv-2604-13555: Acharya, Ale, and Kadel detect phishing sites from screenshots rather than text or web addresses, since fake pages copy logos, layouts, and colors. They compare two vision models, ConvNeXt-Tiny and a Vision Transformer, trained on webpage images with ImageNet starting weights. ConvNeXt-Tiny wins on balance between catches and false alarms and runs more cheaply, and the authors stress tuning the decision threshold for real deployment.
arxiv-2604-13955: Frazier and Damevski tailor code-safety teaching to each student. They plant known weakness types in students' own assignment code. An agentic framework runs the planting, scoring, ranking, and lesson design. The system ran in two college courses with 71 students. Learners called their own-code examples more relevant and engaging than textbook ones. But measured gains over generic materials were small.
arxiv-2604-14155: Angel sets out a canonical normal form for powers of a curved differential within curved differential algebras. The operator calculus avoids heavy combinatorics. From it he gives sharp tests for when curvature constraints force N-complex structures, showing that a nilpotent curvature power still guarantees a strict complex structure of related order. He also treats curvature as a filtration control on a square-zero chain complex, gaining Lipschitz control of barcodes under curvature change, and illustrates the mechanism on a four-vertex flag complex.
arxiv-2604-14255: Gonzalez counts homogeneous colored linear orderings that are countable, in k colors, and also counts countable C-n-m-homogeneous orderings. The C-n-m notion tightens homogeneity toward a recent sp-homogeneity concept with computability-theoretic value. Closed formulas and asymptotic bounds follow for both counts, and the objects, though mostly endless, match finite objects, proving there are only finitely many.
arxiv-2604-14755: Sun, Zhang, Qian, Yang, and Luo built ASGNet for polyp segmentation in colonoscopy images, where varied shapes, busy backgrounds, and hidden polyps defeat local-only vision. A spectrum-guided non-local perception module joins local and global information to sharpen polyp boundaries. A multi-source semantic extractor adds high-level cues for rough localization. A dense cross-layer decoder then fuses layer information into high-quality masks. Across five benchmarks ASGNet beat 21 leading methods. Code will be public.
arxiv-2604-14955: Cipollini and 23 others compare three ways to share a quantum processing unit between quantum and classical work in high-performance computing. Time-based multiplexing, dynamic resource management, and workflow decomposition were tested on production clusters and real quantum hardware. Malleability and workflow strategies cut classical resource use by up to 45.7 percent and 64 percent, suiting jobs with evenly balanced quantum and classical loads. Time-multiplexing instead boosts quantum-unit use and cuts cluster execution time, suiting jobs with strongly imbalanced loads.
arxiv-2604-15055: Valdivia, Cazelles, and Févotte sharpen time-frequency pictures of shifting signals by fusing spectrograms. Each spectrogram trades time sharpness against frequency sharpness, a limit set by the Gabor-Heisenberg principle. Their method blends two or more spectrograms of differing sharpness into one super-resolution view via optimal transport. Unlike older fusion, inputs need not share one time-frequency grid, and the output grid can be set by the user.
arxiv-2604-15255: Murakami, Tang, and Zhang open up real-time multi-spectral photoacoustic imaging with a shared hardware-software architecture. Fast-tuning lasers and non-real-time operating systems often destabilize synchronization between lasers and data capture. Their design pairs an independent microcontroller for deterministic laser trigger counting with a decoupled client-server streaming framework. Built for the widely used OPOTEK Phocus and Verasonics Vantage pairing, it dodges OS timing drift and storage bottlenecks to lower cost and technical barriers.
arxiv-2604-15455: Thompson, Biza, and Konidaris teach robots to transfer a skill to new object shapes from a single demonstration by splitting objects into semantic parts. Data-efficient generative shape models carry interaction points from the demo object's parts to matching parts of a novel object, and an auto-built objective aligns those points on skill-relevant parts. The method succeeds one-shot across varied skills and geometries in simulation and on real robots.
arxiv-2604-15555: Dong and 27 colleagues present the CXR-LT 2026 challenge, a multi-center benchmark for chest X-ray classification under long tails and unseen classes. It draws on more than 145,000 images from PadChest and NIH sets, with development and test sets newly labeled by radiologists. Two tasks follow: robust classification on 30 known classes and open-world generalization to 6 unseen rare diseases. Vision-language foundation models improve both settings, but rare findings under center shift stay hard.
arxiv-2604-15655: Aiki and Higaki show that shut vortex loops can take on screw-like spins that split off from a round loop under the Localized Induction Equation. The new loops stay near the round loop's path yet drift off it bit by bit. Their axial speed differs from the round loop's. The pair write down plain shifts that meet bounds for staying near the orbit yet fail the stricter test of staying put, so the two kinds of steadiness come apart.
arxiv-2604-15855: Liang and 14 colleagues propose PISP, a framework that infers stellar parameters from large spectroscopic datasets better and faster. It builds an orthonormal basis and works in the projected space, easing the damage that linked parameters cause. The basis comes from principal component analysis or the active-subspace method, paired with two fitting approaches to give four versions. Tests on model spectra and 722,896 observed APOGEE spectra show better values for many star traits, plus about 4 times faster inference in the observed-data case.
arxiv-2604-15955: Bürk and three colleagues run particle-resolved simulation of turbulent open channel flow past a vertical cylinder on a smooth wall, with mobile heavy round particles. The cylinder spawns intense swirls, stronger wake turbulence, and sharp changes in wall shear stress. These shifts reshape mean particle concentration, with build-up and depletion across the wake and stronger upward transport against gravity. Adding wall roughness boosts entrainment further, giving the rough-wall-plus-cylinder setup the largest share of entrained particles, even far from the wall.
arxiv-2604-16255: Green, Holmes, and Im generalise the rooted-tree link to k-tuples of functions across k disjoint vertex sets. They give a weighted tally of eventually constant k-tuples, which settle to constancy under repeated composition. Identifying these tuples with their induced digraphs, they give explicit formulas for generating polynomials and analyse their cardinality. The polynomials are multisymmetric in k variable sets, and can be restated as a character of a representation of a product of general linear groups.
arxiv-2604-16355: Anžel, Yang, and Hattab improve summary polar diagrams, including Taylor and mutual information diagrams, which reveal relationships, data similarity, and correspondence. While polar diagrams remain indispensable for some tasks, their polar nature can hinder intuitiveness and cause overplotting. Their hybrid approach combines small multiples, overview plus detail, aggregation, interactive filtering, and Cartesian linking. A user study finds comparable response times among participants, and three domain experts reviewed an implementation across climate, data science, and machine learning cases.
arxiv-2604-16555: Yoshimura and colleagues propose LLMasTool, a tree frame for neural design search. Code search relies on hand-crafted spaces that limit open work. Language-model methods reduce manual design but struggle to make designs and show training-data biases. LLMasTool pulls modules from source code and represents designs as layered trees. Growth proceeds through tree changes, not code writing, with diverse Bayesian planning at coarse level. The model settles degrees of freedom, giving a working design and a path. It beats methods by 0.69, 1.83 and 2.68 on CIFAR-10, CIFAR-100 and ImageNet16-120.
arxiv-2604-16655: Zhang and colleagues build a multi-modal MRI framework for brain age prediction lifespan. Existing approaches cover narrow age ranges and single-modality data, missing structural change. Their model processes modalities, then fuses them late in both stages. Stage one estimates a probability distribution over six stages; stage two predicts age through weighted specialist experts. On nine sets from fetal onward, it cuts average error by 13 percent and 78 percent over rivals. Combining modalities adds 12 to 13 percent gains, and ADNI results suggest the brain age gap tracks Alzheimer's-related aging.
arxiv-2604-16755: Kriegmair and Wulff ask whether behavioral differences among language models reflect stable individuality or global response biases and noise. They apply crossed random-effects models from psychometrics to seventy-four point nine million ratings from 10 open-weight models. The ratings cover over 100,000 words across 14 psycholinguistic norms. On average about 17 percent of variance traces to stimulus-specific individuality, beating a statistical null model clearly. Cross-norm prediction shows individuality as a coherent fingerprint for each model, not attributable to bias or noise.
arxiv-2604-16855: Li and colleagues study post-training W4A4 quantization of camouflaged object detection. Predictions rest on subtle texture and boundary cues, and background tokens dominate a shared activation range. That domination inflates the step size and pushes weak boundary cues into the zero bin. COD-TDQ answers with two steps: token-group scales suppressing cross-token domination, and range projection bounding step ratio and zero-bin mass. Across four benchmarks and two baselines, COD-TDQ scores more than zero point one two higher than the leading quantization method without retraining.
arxiv-2604-17355: Basumallick and three colleagues survey weak gravitational lensing, the bending of light by curved spacetime that exposes massive objects indirectly. Starting from the Newtonian approximation, they develop the lens equation and lensing potential, then interpret light paths through Fermat's principle with an effective refractive index. Photon motion is traced through spherical geometries and the equatorial plane of spinning Kerr black holes, and bending angles are checked by the Rindler-Ishak method and the Gauss-Bonnet theorem. The survey closes by extending the picture to axisymmetric spacetimes.
arxiv-2604-17555: Zeng and four colleagues argue that agentic search stalls because its retrieval system stays frozen while only the reasoning agent learns. Their CoSearch framework trains a multi-step reasoning agent together with a generative document ranker through Group Relative Policy Optimization. A preliminary test put the gap between an oracle retriever and a fixed one at up to 26.8 percent relative F1 across seven question-answering benchmarks. Joint training with a semantic grouping strategy steadies ranker learning across shifting reasoning paths, aiming to close that gap.
arxiv-2604-17955: Kobayashi and four colleagues identify a bypass that lets bar-driven gas reach galactic centers despite the nuclear ring where inflow usually stalls. In three-dimensional simulations, a fraction of inflowing gas gains vertical momentum, vaults across the ring, and arrives in the inner few tens of parsecs. The reaching material starts outside the ring, beyond about 300 parsecs, and needs a vertical excursion near 100 parsecs before the ring plus substantial loss of azimuthal angular momentum. Most gas still piles into the ring, but the vaulting stream feeds the central disk.
arxiv-2604-18455: Gkeneralis studies equivariant rigidity of complex and quaternionic moment-angle manifolds. Cutting the problem down to their quasitoric or quoric quotients with main bundle frames, he proves complex moment-angle ones are rigid in the homeomorphism sense. Any closed locally linear manifold with the same shape matches it as a space. Under Hopkinson's global rule, the second case gains the same rigidity, so homotopy type settles homeomorphism type in this setting.
arxiv-2604-18655: Kodavanti and 15 colleagues present a chip-aware frame for running a LLaMA-based multilingual base model on phones. App-tuned LoRAs feed in at run time to one frozen graph, so tasks can swap with no rebuild and no added memory. A multi-stream decoder turns out style variants in one pass, cutting wait times by up to 6 times. Dynamic Self-Speculative Decoding speeds token output by up to 2.3 times. With INT4 quantization and design tweaks, the whole system gains 4 to 6 times on memory and wait times.
arxiv-2604-18755: Dubovskaya, O'Sullivan, and Quayle build an agent-based model of opinion polarization. Agents balance two drives: standing out in their local group and simplifying the overall opinion landscape, both scored with Shannon entropy. Pairs of agents meet and decide whether to adopt each other's views under these opposing pressures. The mix reproduces distinct heterogeneous opinion clusters, with views still shifting after clusters form. Polarization arises when local groups are moderate in size, while smaller groups fragment and larger ones block distinct clusters.
arxiv-2604-18955: Davoudi and four colleagues present the first broad evaluation of modern language models on social media analytics. They test authorship verification, post generation, and user attribute inference on a Twitter data set. For authorship checks, they sample widely and test on fresh tweets from January 2024 onward to limit seen data bias. A user study gauges how real users judge model posts written in their own style. Attribute labels use standard job taxonomies, and the work sets reproducible benchmarks for the field.
arxiv-2604-19455: Revathi, Thirisangu, and Subramani present an acoustofluidic method for taming Rayleigh-Taylor instability, which arises when a dense fluid sits atop a lighter fluid and gravity drives chaotic mixing. Standing bulk acoustic waves counteract the instability and suppress mixing. Suppression needs two conditions at once: the acoustic energy density must exceed its critical threshold, and the waves must run perpendicular to the fluid-fluid interface. The method cuts the mixing index by up to an order of magnitude versus gravity-driven mixing alone.
arxiv-2604-20055: Vossler and eleven colleagues scale quality improvement with AI, formalizing fuzzy, iterative factor discovery. Current alignment assumes well-defined tasks, but factor discovery is iterative sense-making from expert judgment, fishbones, chart reviews, and Lean methods. Their Human-AI Spec-Solution Co-optimization treats specs as tunable settings, refined by experts and agents until extractions match expert notes. At a safety-net hospital, the pipeline reached at least 70 percent match on long stays and unplanned 30-day returns, matched prior findings, added new factors, and left clear traces.
arxiv-2604-20455: Ahmad studies how strategic interaction can arise from steered quantum motion rather than from outside math. He sets out quantum games defined by interaction, where players are distinct quantum walkers, choices are local coin steps, and payoffs are means of observables. Using interacting discrete-time quantum walks, he shows by simulation that competitive, cooperative, and asymmetric games can reach stable steady plans when walkers are coupled, while no nontrivial equilibria exist without interaction. An analysis of weak couplings shows strategic coupling comes from interference terms caused by interaction.
arxiv-2604-20655: Lei, Fabila Carrasco, and Escudero offer a graph version of Sample Entropy, called SampEn-G, to measure roughness of graph signals. Instead of time delay maps, their approach uses multi-hop graph-based maps, pooling patterns from walk-weighted means via powers of the graph shift operator. They show that SampEn-G reduces to standard 1D Sample Entropy on path graphs, and test its sensitivity with the logistic map. Tests on Erdos-Renyi signals show its shape with links and pattern length, at times for thousands of nodes.
arxiv-2604-20855: Liang, Meyerson, and Miikkulainen build Caesar, an agent that moves past flat web retrieval toward creative discovery. It traverses the web to assemble a changing knowledge graph, then uses that graph to steer toward varied, less obvious sources. A second stage refines drafts adversarially, seeking fresh angles rather than confirming prior views. In creative synthesis tests it beats leading deep-research agents by 13 to 23 percent.
arxiv-2604-20955: Dambal and Bittner probe how a chaotic Tavis-Cummings cavity, where light and matter states blend, settles toward thermal balance. They use the eigenstate thermalization hypothesis, which links single quantum states to thermal traits. At weak coupling, a non-integrable excitonic Hamiltonian drives local thermalization through chaos. At strong coupling, that chaos is damped and thermalization stalls. The split shapes photon counts, and the pair point to entangled-biphoton tests as a way to probe the hidden disorder.
arxiv-2604-21255: Chenghao Yang and six colleagues measure how distillation makes AI agents behave alike, separating required task behaviors from freely chosen habits. Their two metrics track verbal alignment and tool-use habits as directed graphs. Across 18 models from 8 providers on tau-bench tasks, same-family pairs score higher on tool-use similarity than cross-family pairs, and Kimi-K2 even exceeds Anthropic's own Opus on node and dependency similarity. A controlled distillation test confirms the metrics catch teacher-specific convergence rather than general improvement.
arxiv-2604-21555: Paul Keuren, Marc Ponsen, and Robert Ayoub Bagheri propose Concept Separation Curves, a classifier-free way to evaluate embeddings. Most tests rely on classifiers or downstream tasks, leaving unclear whether good results come from embedding or classifier. Their approach adds syntactic noise and negations to sentences, then gauges effects on the embeddings. Plotting effects as Concept Separation Curves shows how a model splits conceptual from surface variations. Tests across domains, in Dutch and English, and lengths show the curves offer a reproducible way to judge conceptual stability across models.
arxiv-2604-21755: Liu and four colleagues trace how a sound speed that differs from the usual value during inflation reshapes quantum-information marks left in the early universe. They follow tiny ripples in the early cosmos, known as cosmological perturbations, using a two-mode squeezed-state setup. A changing sound speed alters how squeezing evolves, and those changes pass into the state of the part we can observe. It lowers purity, boosts entropy and entanglement measures, and delays the onset of classicality by slowing decoherence.
arxiv-2604-21955: Guerrero casts quantum circuit design as a four-player potential game. Its state is a graph, and its players encode trainability, non-stabilizerness, performance, and hardware cost. Moves factorise into append, remove, retype, and rewire. A sweep on MaxCut K4 traces a frontier from Clifford to non-Clifford. On three topologies, Nash search achieves the highest mean potential, reaching the ceiling on the 2 by 2 grid. On LiH/STO-3G, Nash seeded from a Givens-doubles ansatz produces a 48-operation, depth-25 circuit retaining 97.7 percent of correlation energy.
arxiv-2604-22055: Wang and Han present a swap MCMC method linking a tied chain moving on a hidden manifold with a loose helper chain set in a tube around the constraint. In real cases, surfaces are sometimes disconnected from tricky shapes forced by bent rules. The loose chain lets the sampler jump between disconnected parts. The authors show the result samples a wider set of hidden manifolds, even disconnected ones. They prove the sampler meets balance, ergodicity, and convergence.
arxiv-2604-22255: Singh, Pandey and Karmakar study X-ray coronae, the hot outer atmospheres, of three active K-type stars. Quiet coronae fit two-temperature plasma models, with a cool part around 0.3 keV and a hot part near 1 keV. Spectra show iron depleted by factors of 5 to 10, plus an inverse first-ionisation-potential effect in all three. Six flares qualify as superflares, with peaks from 30 to 133 MK. LQ Hya shows repeat superflares at the same rotational phase six months apart, hinting at a long-lived, complex magnetic structure.
arxiv-2604-22455: Alman, Cohen, Gal, Maggi and Montali present the ABPMS frame as a hybrid form. The frame sets outer limits for the system, more permissive than old models, enabling framed autonomy. The authors model it as procedural and declarative models side by side, extending the open-world assumption across types. Non-clashing models can combine for execution, but discovery from event data is hard for models relying on directly-follows relations. They analyse how one type's behaviours appear as Declare constraints matching eventually-follows relations, revealing overlaps for future discovery.
arxiv-2604-22555: Dasanaike and Imai improve race prediction for people whose surnames the Census does not cover. Researchers often use Bayesian Improved Surname Geocoding, which leans on Census surname tables. Those tables miss uncommon surnames, leaving out about 10 percent of the United States population. Standard BISG then falls back on a flat generic prior for such names, degrading predictions. Their embedding-powered BISG instead represents names as dense vectors from pretrained text embeddings and trains neural networks on 2020 Census surname and first-name data.
arxiv-2604-22655: Zirkind and Diehl present the Associativity Peakiness metric, a single score for contingency tables. To compare clustering tools, one metric for table outputs is needed, yet prior work found none. Scores exist for true and guessed value pairs, another clustering output form, but they miss detail visible in contingency tables. The AP metric captures the performance traits that matter for predicting how a clustering tool will do once deployed. It is akin to quality measures for confusion matrices from supervised learning, and the paper gives test results.
arxiv-2604-23055: Peterson and Jacquart use inelasticity reconstruction to sharpen mass ordering studies with IceCube. Earth's matter affects atmospheric neutrino oscillations differently, and more neutrinos than antineutrinos reach IceCube. Inelasticity, the energy fraction passed to the nucleon in an event, differs between neutrinos and antineutrinos by chirality, which allows stats-based splits. Two new methods, built with a graph neural network and an ensemble of convolutional networks, add inelasticity as a fourth observable with energy, path, and flavor to gauge reach.
arxiv-2604-23655: Huang and colleagues present BVI-Mamba, a video enhancement framework for low-light and underwater footage built on a visual state-space model instead of transformers or convolutions. One module aligns features across frames in space and time, while a second removes noise and adjusts brightness through a UNet-style network with state-space blocks. It beats transformer and convolution baselines on both low-light and underwater tasks while using less memory and time.
arxiv-2604-23855: Borovkov and six colleagues deploy a system that automates enterprise customer-support workflows inside a business process platform. It learns a next-action policy from interface traces, trains a critic on copilot feedback to set abstention levels, and runs only high-confidence steps in the background, deferring uncertain calls to operators. One operator can thus supervise many sessions at once. In production it automated 45 percent of sessions and cut handling time by nearly two-fifths with no quality loss.
arxiv-2604-23955: Smith reviews hard-probe data in ultraperipheral collisions at LHCb, where quarkonia production probes photon links, nuclear parton structure, and vector-meson yields. It sets the most precise readings against the latest theory models. It also presents new rho(770) and phi(1020) vector meson studies at forward angles, set against other results, and covers future ultraperipheral work with the new LHCb device in Run 3.
arxiv-2604-24055: Nakano and Sakai study spin excitations in a frustrated Heisenberg antiferromagnet that moves from a bounce lattice through a maple-leaf lattice to an exact-dimer system. Using large parallel numerical diagonalization, they track the excitation gap above the ground state for spin one-half and spin one. Both cases stay gapped at small coupling ratios and turn gapless near a ratio of about 1.4, with a second gapped region appearing for spin one beyond that point.
arxiv-2604-24255: Schanne and five colleagues overview the ECLAIRs trigger aboard the French-Chinese SVOM satellite, launched in mid-2024 to study transients, chiefly gamma-ray bursts. The onboard trigger detects and localizes bursts and requests slews so narrow-field MXT and VT can follow up. It also sends real-time alerts through the VHF network for rapid follow-up. Two onboard algorithms, the Count-Rate Trigger and the Image Trigger, issue sky-localized alerts, and the trigger has caught classical and X-ray-rich bursts, enabling redshift measurements.
arxiv-2604-24955: Tu and six colleagues build BenchGuard, a tool that audits LLM agent benchmarks. Many seeming agent failures are really benchmark flaws: broken specs, hidden assumptions and rigid scoring. BenchGuard cross-checks all benchmark parts with LLM protocols, optionally using agent solutions. On ScienceAgentBench it found 12 author-confirmed issues, including fatal errors that made tasks unsolvable. It matched 83.3 percent of expert-found issues on the BIXBench Verified-50 subset, catching flaws human review missed. A full audit of 50 bioinformatics tasks costs under 15 dollars.
arxiv-2604-25055: Pereyra furthers the study of graph unimodularity through Kőnig-Egerváry graphs. He introduces a new factorization inside the Kőnig-Egerváry class. Partitioning vertices into perfect-flower and perfect-flower-free parts, he proves it factors into two determinants. The two factors belong to the two induced subgraphs. He obtains the analogous result for the permanent. The decomposition reduces it to two very different subgraphs. One ties to Sterboul-Deming patterns with perfect matching; the other follows critical independent sets.
arxiv-2604-25155: Zhao and seven colleagues argue that wireless communications suits formal AI reasoning well. Math has long grounded wireless theory, but new systems demand harder reasoning from experts. AI advances in theorem proving and language-model derivation offer a promising but largely unexplored path. The authors propose a three-layer framework of verification, derivation and discovery. The domain is structured, the authors say, so proofs can be checked step by step.
arxiv-2604-25455: Ryskeldiev argues generative UI can bridge C2C accessibility gaps. User-made content breaks the static model: blurry photos, missing size and condition notes, and shifting page structure. Drawing on six 2022 to 2025 studies with blind, low-vision, and older C2C users, he shows generative UI can adapt interfaces at use. Three interventions: HTML regeneration for screen readers, guidance for older sellers, and audio-guided framing for blind sellers. For HCI practice, generative UI goes beyond the screen, complements ability-based design, and shifts designers to policies.
arxiv-2604-25755: Scharf and seven colleagues test tensor networks for classifying objects in synthetic aperture radar images, which suffer heavy noise and a wide dynamic range. Deploying such models on drones and military aircraft also demands small models that stay accurate. Unlike earlier work focused on conventional neural networks for radar detection, this study stresses robustness and model reduction. The findings show tensor networks handle both robustness, including resilience to data poisoning, and efficiency. They offer a lean alternative for radar classification on edge devices.
arxiv-2604-26155: Ramos, Hulak, and de Queiroz pin down the field-sensitive part of the split Levi image for exterior spinors where two is invertible. The spin-to-orthogonal map's kernel is plus and minus one, so the exterior action descends only projectively. For the split line the image is the square-scaling subgroup. Clifford representatives, a weight-two torus conjugation law, and a lifting rule for square determinants cover arbitrary split rank. In rank at least three, the spin image meets the split Levi subgroup exactly in its square-determinant part.
arxiv-2604-26255: Li and seven colleagues built GaitKD, a teaching framework that helps small gait-recognition models learn from large ones. Walking style identifies people at a distance without contact, but strong models are often too heavy to run in practice. GaitKD splits the lesson in two: matching the teacher's decisions and keeping its boundary layout in the student's embedding space. The split design works across mixed teacher-student pairs and adds no cost at run time.
arxiv-2604-26355: Zhao and three colleagues compressed language-model reasoning with entropy-guided supertokens, merges learned from a model's own reasoning traces. Reasoning tokens split into low-entropy scaffolding phrases and higher-entropy problem-specific content, so cross-word merges capture frequent structural patterns for fine-tuning. Traces shrank by about 8 percent on average across model families and math benchmarks, with accuracy equivalent or inconclusive in most cells. Learned supertokens also mapped onto moves like backtracking, verification, and strategy shifts.
arxiv-2604-26955: Olowe and Chitnis describe a routing and governance system for AI tutors in engineering labs, balancing help against learning. Routiium, an OpenAI-compatible gateway, manages multiple language-model backends with configurable prompts and logs, while EduRouter enforces per-lab budgets, approval workflows, and embedding-based question matching. In simulations from two labs, governed policies lifted challenge alignment and overlay adherence over ungoverned operation, and stretched the struggle window before scaffold hints appeared. A 100-query replay sent 75 percent of queries to a local model, cutting token costs by 66 percent.
arxiv-2604-27155: Silva, Adnan, Dangel, and Oore recast model merging as Frechet averaging on a chosen manifold. Merging joins trained models into one with no further training. Plain averaging of weights breaks when the same model can be written in more than one way. So both the shape of the space and the averaging rule must respect those swaps. Merged weights sit as close as they can to all source models at once. This view contains Fisher merging, with a case for low-rank adapters.
arxiv-2604-27355: Gould and five colleagues compute a certified outer bound on the minimizers of a strongly convex task with shaky, capped cost inputs. They treat each descent step as part of an uncertain dynamical system, with the cost input held fixed yet unknown, and follow where its reachable sets lead. Exponential convergence to each parameter's minimizer turns those sets into bounds on the whole minimizer set, and the error fades exponentially as steps pile up. They tune the step sequence with system-level synthesis and beat baselines with low conservativeness.
arxiv-2604-27655: Baird studies sigma-algebra systems ordered by refinement and defines endogenous chance measures, stable under allowed changes. He proves such measures exist on finite systems and describes their structure. Refinement steps then induce a natural changing structure on the sigma-algebra lattice. The work links order, measure, and dynamics in these finite systems.
arxiv-2604-27755: Fang and Ma introduce Gårding polynomials, multi-variable polynomials whose positivity zones stay put under positive shifts and positive affine maps. They prove this shape matches both a multi-affine cut via polarization and a test using partial derivatives. The class strictly widens real stable polynomials while keeping their structure, including the Rayleigh property for non-negative multi-affine cases. It also holds for matroid generating functions under natural matroid moves, yielding fresh negative-dependence results past real-stability methods. Matching results follow for certain matrix characteristic polynomials.
arxiv-2604-28155: Brattegard's team studies temperature sensing with a finite reservoir, where heat exchange with a quantum dot shifts its own heat. They compare three strategies in the long-time limit. The first tracks quanta swapped with it, the second reads total current into an infinite reservoir, and the third reads dot occupation. Fisher information for all three shares common factors from the finite reservoir, and tracking swapped quanta proves optimal, with gate voltage tuning maximal precision within each strategy.
arxiv-2605-00655:
Constantine Theocharis and Edwin Brady reformulate type theory with erasure, the feature that lets a proof assistant delete irrelevant data at compile time. Many systems, including Agda, Idris, and Rocq, implement some version of it, since proofs and specifications should not slow down the running program. The authors present a structural version, written as a second-order generalized algebraic theory, where erasure becomes a phase distinction between runtime and erased terms.

The formulation buys several advantages: models based on categories with families, compatibility with features such as staging, and a clearer guideline for implementers. They prove conservativity over Martin-Löf type theory in both phases, so the extension proves nothing new about ordinary terms. For code extraction, a presheaf model produces untyped lambda programs, with correctness proved by gluing. Everything is formalized in Agda, with a toy elaborator included.
arxiv-2605-00855:
Wei-Ting Tang, Akshay Kudva, Calvin Tsay, and Joel A. Paulson study how to find the true global optimum of a trained Gaussian process model's posterior mean over a box-shaped domain. The mean has a compact formula, yet it stays nonlinear and nonconvex, and exact methods scale poorly as training data grows. Approximate methods gain speed by changing the objective, which loses exactness.

Their PALM-Mean method builds piecewise-analytic lower bounds inside a reduced-space branch-and-bound search. Locally important kernel terms get a sign-aware piecewise-linear relaxation, while the rest are bounded in closed form. The authors prove valid bounds and convergence to a global optimum within tolerance. Benchmarks show better scaling than general-purpose deterministic solvers as data size grows.
arxiv-2605-00955:
Zelin Guan and six co-authors propose E-MIA, an exam-style black-box attack that tests whether a document sits inside a retrieval-augmented generation system's knowledge base. That corpus is a sensitive asset, and membership can leak coverage of sensitive topics. Earlier attacks rely on soft similarity signals with unstable thresholds, or on obvious confirmation probes that invite refusal and detection.

E-MIA turns verifiable details in a candidate document, such as names, definitions, and causal relations, into objectively gradable exam questions of four types. The combined score across evidence-targeted questions serves as the membership signal. Across datasets and system configurations, separability improves in stringent settings while queries stay natural and stealthy. Question mix and exam length effects are also analyzed.
arxiv-2605-01555:
Arnau Marin-Llobet and Javier Ferrando automate the detective work of mechanistic interpretability, the effort to say what single neurons and features inside a language model actually do. Hand labeling is slow, and one-shot machine labels are often vague stories that no test could refute.

Their multi-agent system runs two linked loops. In one, an agent proposes rival explanations for a feature and refines them with targeted prompt controls and several scoring metrics. In the other, an agent builds prompt sets, graphs activations by closeness, and pulls out candidate features using separability and coherence tests. Tested on the Gemma-2 family and on sparse transformer neurons, the system beats one-shot auto-labels, finds language-specific and safety-relevant features, and leaves an audit trail for each claim. The authors argue that loops of testable guesses beat single confident labels.
arxiv-2605-01755:
Adenane Rim, Avram Florin, Miruna Beldiman, and Halanay Andrei-Dan partition the fate of multi-strain epidemics. Their framework covers reaction network models where several strains share one host pool through bilinear infection blocks that do not interact. It asks the global questions: does the disease die out, does one strain exclude the rest, or can strains persist together?

The engine is a Perron-Volterra Lyapunov function, a certificate built from Perron eigenvectors of the boundary dynamics and entropy terms for strains. Five pillars support it: siphon sets that mark invariant faces, Metzler Jacobians on those faces, next-generation matrices from splittings, invasion relays at eigenvalue crossings, and the Lyapunov build itself. The parameter space splits into at most one more region than there are strains, each owned by extinction or one dominant strain, with coexistence confined to tie surfaces of equal reproduction numbers. A Mathematica package automates the construction.
arxiv-2605-01855:
Frédéric Déglise, Niels Feld, and Fangzhou Jin construct Gysin pullbacks with full homotopy coherence for weak Borel-Moore theories on smooth schemes. Gysin maps handle pullback along closed immersions and related factorisations, but making all higher compatibilities cohere is a known hard problem in motivic homotopy theory. Their construction starts from higher deformation spaces attached to flags of closed immersions.

From those spaces they build higher Gysin simplices and their simplicial identities, up to contractible choices. A rigidification step then turns the coherent system into a strict contravariant simplicial functor that extends both smooth pullbacks and closed-immersion Gysin maps. As an application, Rost-Schmid complexes over general bases form weak Borel-Moore theories and are represented by motivic objects from the construction.
arxiv-2605-02255:
Karima Makhlouf and colleagues run a unified ablation study of privacy attacks on large language models. Past studies usually test one attack at a time, which gives little guidance on which system factors drive risk. The authors build one threat model and test four attacks: membership inference, attribute inference, data extraction, and backdoor attacks.

Each attack responds to different factors. Membership inference depends strongly on data traits and attack strategy, while attribute inference follows model and training traits. Data extraction grows with model scale and with repetition of training data. Backdoor attacks succeed at consistently high rates. From those patterns, the authors derive practical advice for privacy-aware deployment, such as checking membership leakage in retrieval systems and limiting repeated personal data.
arxiv-2605-02355:
Sarah Roth, Sven Jäger, Niels Lindner, and Anita Schöbel design periodic railway timetables that save energy without punishing passengers. Braking trains can regenerate energy, but only if another train accelerates at the right moment, and timetables that maximise that overlap are often bad for travel time. The authors formulate a two-criteria optimisation that extends the Periodic Event Scheduling Problem.

Their model maximises regenerated energy, measured as brake-traction overlap time, and minimises passenger travel time at once. They study computational complexity on one-station networks, using matchings and Hamiltonian paths. The problem is hard even for one objective alone, yet several special cases admit polynomial-time solutions. Two case studies test practicality and map the Pareto front between energy and time.
arxiv-2605-02455:
Shuzhao Feng and three co-authors tackle a weak spot in code generation: models write single functions well, but quality drops for whole software projects held in one repository. In their view, plain text prompts are too vague for that scale, and the results are hard to check. They propose structured spec-driven engineering, where formal spec files guide the model.

A pilot study tests the idea on the business logic of three systems, using five large language models in a common model-view-controller layout. From the pilot, the authors draw lessons on what helps, what blocks progress, and what should come next. Their claim is modest: with clear specs, project-scale generation becomes a real goal, and its output becomes easier to verify.
arxiv-2605-02655:
Zhian Jia introduces temporal state tomography, a framework for reconstructing quantum processes that unfold across several times. Standard tomography rebuilds a state or a channel from measurements. Multi-time processes are richer, and their full description needs a joint account of what happens at each step and how steps connect.

The framework rests on temporal quasiprobability distributions, which in the complete setting fully describe a multi-time process and fix a temporal state. Jia shows that any such distribution can be obtained by classical post-processing of outcomes from one fixed set of quantum instruments, giving an experimental route to the data. A Bloch-type representation then rebuilds the temporal state. Sample complexity is derived, stating how many measurements the method needs for a given accuracy.
arxiv-2605-02755:
J. Lisenfeld and three co-authors trace a readout failure in superconducting qubits back to a material defect in the qubit's tunnel junction. Defects form parasitic two-level systems that are a major source of decoherence, the loss of quantum behavior. Here one such defect couples strongly to a transmon qubit from inside its barrier.

Using multi-photon spectroscopy and strain tuning of the defect, the team explores the joint system of defect, qubit, and readout resonator. The defect couples resonantly to the resonator itself, dressing its states and shifting its frequency, which spoils the readout signal. No amount of better electronics fixes a shifted resonator. The finding adds one more concrete route by which material flaws can block solid-state quantum processors.
arxiv-2605-03255:
Anna Sokol, Marianna B. Ganapini, and Nitesh V. Chawla ask whether large language models hold core beliefs, the stable commitments that anchor a human worldview. A core belief resists debunking because dropping it would reshape how one sees reality itself.

Using adversarial dialogue trees across science, history, geography, biology, and mathematics, they press models to defend key claims under sustained challenge. Most models failed to hold a stable worldview, and even recent, steadier models eventually gave way under conversational pressure. Argument skill has clearly grown across generations, the authors find, but a core-belief structure still appears absent.
arxiv-2605-03455:
David González Méndez, Rubén Gómez González, and Vicente Garzó derive transport properties for a confined granular fluid driven by a stochastic bath with friction. Granular flows of grains or powders lose energy in collisions, so steady states need external driving, here modeled through a gas phase with drag and random kicks.

Extending the delta collision model within Enskog kinetic theory, they apply the Chapman-Enskog method to get viscosity, thermal conductivity, and cooling rate analytically. Steady temperature and kurtosis predictions match Monte Carlo simulations closely. Driving changes the transport coefficients markedly versus dry systems, and the steady state proves linearly stable throughout.
arxiv-2605-03755:
Gülşen Doğan and Ümit Akıncı simulate meron lattices in synthetic antiferromagnets, layered materials that can host fractional topological textures called merons and antimerons. Ferromagnets struggle to hold such textures steady, so synthetic antiferromagnet bilayers with easy-plane anisotropy are the platform. The authors use large-scale Monte Carlo runs to watch the crystal order change.

In a single uncoupled layer, stronger anisotropy shrinks meron cores and breaks the lattice symmetry from fourfold to twofold. An ultra-weak antiferromagnetic coupling between layers acts as a scaffold: it locks the layers together into bimeron dipoles and restores the fourfold symmetry. Even where crystalline order collapses at extreme anisotropy, the coupling keeps a strict local topological locking.
arxiv-2605-03955:
Elisa Davoli, Alberto Fanizza, and Marco Picerni generalize the Maz'ya-Shaposhnikova formula. It is a classical result. It describes what fractional Sobolev seminorms converge to as the fractional parameter tends to zero. The classical formula assumes functions in the square-integrable class, which forces vanishing at infinity. Many natural functions fail that assumption, leaving a gap the authors set out to close.

By introducing a notion of mass at infinity, they pin down the limit of Gagliardo seminorms localized on a bounded Lipschitz domain. They count only pairs with at least one point inside the domain. The limiting functional unifies the picture. It reduces to the ordinary norm for globally integrable functions. It recovers the pointwise limit of fractional perimeters for characteristic functions. It also encodes the limiting behavior in the sense of Gamma-convergence. A version for metric measure spaces follows.
arxiv-2605-04055:
JiangBo Zhao and ZhaoXin Liu propose MetaAdamW, a meta-learned optimizer that adapts its own settings per parameter group.
